fields.features_heading: What Each Proposal Carries When It Arrives
fields.features_subheading: A proposal missing its price sheet sends the buyer back to the vendor. These six pieces make each one complete when it lands.
fields.feature_1:
Technical and price proposals, filed apart

Ask for the technical proposal and the price proposal as two separate uploads. Evaluators read the approach first and open the pricing only after their technical scores are saved.
fields.feature_2:
A signed offer on every submission

The vendor's authorized signer types a name and signs before the proposal goes in. The signature, the signer's title, and the time of signing are saved with the uploaded files.
fields.feature_3:
Required files before submit works

Mark the insurance certificate and each addendum acknowledgment as required. A vendor who skips one sees which file is missing and cannot submit until that file is attached.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for each proposal that arrives

The buyer gets an email or a Slack message when a proposal comes in. Evaluators get a reminder 2 days before their score sheets are due, and a late sheet escalates to the buyer.
fields.feature_5:
Proposals stored in a database you own

Every proposal and every score is a row in a database you own, with no response caps. Filter by RFP number to see which vendors submitted and at what time, for the procurement file.
fields.feature_6:
The full codebase, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the form on your own servers. An agency with its own hosting rules can keep the procurement portal in house.

fields.usecase_heading: Where an RFP Form Does the Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Nothing after 2:00 PM gets into the proposal file

RFP 26-014 closes at 2:00 PM on its due date. Winslade Unified School District is buying bus routing software, and the technical and price files come in as 2 separate uploads. Corrado Route Systems submits at 1:42 PM and gets a timed receipt. At 2:00 PM the submit button turns off for every vendor.
fields.tab_content_2:
After the cutoff, 14 answers go to all 9 vendors

The question period for the playground job at Bexley Parks ends at a set cutoff. Six vendors send 14 questions through the form, and each lands in one log for Ines Baird, the buyer. She answers them there. The addendum then goes by email to all 9 registered vendors, including those who never asked.
fields.tab_content_3:
Felix sees any request of $50,000 or more

A lab manager at Cordova Community Health needs a new reagent supplier and fills in the RFP request form with the scope and an estimate of $85,000 a year. Any request of $50,000 or more goes to Felix, the procurement director, as a Slack message. Smaller requests wait in the buyers' queue.
fields.tab_content_4:
Quillan Harbor Tech leads at 87 after three evaluators score

Three proposals came in for the gate cameras at Ferrand Port Authority. Evaluators score technical approach out of 40, experience out of 30, and price out of 30, and the app averages the three score sheets. Quillan Harbor Tech averages 34, 26, and 27 for a total of 87. The next proposal sits at 79.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an RFP Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an RFP form that takes complete proposals by the due time and gets them scored, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the goods or services you need and the date the contract should start. Those two answers decide the sections of the form and how long the RFP stays open. Describe both to Emergent in plain English, and it builds the form along with its database.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give the technical approach and the price their own uploads, matching the sections evaluators read. Put a short company profile at the top. Every submission then names the vendor and a contact before anyone opens a file.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the minute and the time zone proposals are due before you add a single field. Write both into the RFP and onto the form itself. Decide now whether a late proposal is refused outright or held for a review.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give questions their own form with a cutoff a week or more before proposals are due. Number each addendum you send, then add a checkbox to the proposal form where the vendor confirms it received every addendum by number.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the buyer an email or a Slack alert for every proposal that arrives. Hold the evaluators' score sheets until the deadline passes, and remind any evaluator whose sheet is still open 2 days before scores are due.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Copy the criteria and weights you published into the score sheet, unchanged. A federal RFP states the factors used to evaluate proposals and their relative importance, and vendors write their proposals to those factors. Changing the weights later breaks that promise.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test proposal 1 minute before a practice deadline and another 1 minute after it. Check that the first one gets a receipt and the second is refused. Then open the record and confirm both files and the signature are attached.

faq_plan.a: An RFP form is the online form vendors use to answer a request for proposals. It takes the company details, the proposal files, and a signed certification before the due time. In federal purchasing, RFPs are used in negotiated acquisitions to communicate Government requirements to prospective contractors and to solicit proposals.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an RFP form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the RFP to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: what you are buying and when proposals are due. Emergent builds the form with its database and the receipt each vendor gets. Change any part by asking for it in the same chat. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What should an RFP form template include?
faq_plan.a: Start with five parts: company details with a contact, the technical proposal, the price proposal as its own upload, an addendum acknowledgment, and a signed certification. Keep those five fixed in the template. For each new purchase, change only the RFP number and the due time.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse an RFP form for other kinds of proposals?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as a buyer is still choosing among written offers, as in a grant round or a consulting engagement. RFP forms carry over well to both. When the request asks companies to pay for exposure at an event, a sponsorship form with packages and tiers fits better than proposal uploads.

faq_plan.q: How long should an RFP form stay open for proposals?
faq_plan.a: For a large federal contract, at least 30 days. Federal agencies shall allow at least a 30-day response time for receipt of bids or proposals when the contract is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. For a private purchase, set the window by how much work a good proposal takes, and print the exact due time on the form.

faq_plan.q: How do I handle vendor questions on an RFP form fairly?
faq_plan.a: Send every answer to every registered vendor at once, as a numbered addendum. Federal rules set the bar: information needed to prepare proposals that is disclosed to one or more potential offerors must be made available to the public as soon as practicable, to avoid an unfair competitive advantage. Leave out the name of the vendor who asked.

faq_plan.q: Can vendors sign up for an RFP site visit through the same form?
faq_plan.a: They can, but a separate booking form works better for it. Vendors pick one of the open visit slots, and each slot closes once it is full. Link to it from the RFP page, and keep the attendee list with the proposal records so evaluators can see who walked the site.

faq_plan.q: What should an RFP form do with a proposal that arrives late?
faq_plan.a: Refuse it at the form and keep a record of the attempt. In federal purchasing, a proposal received after the exact time specified for receipt of proposals is late and will not be considered, with narrow exceptions. A private buyer sets its own rule. Whichever you choose, write it into the RFP and apply it to every vendor.

faq_plan.q: How should evaluators compare scores from RFP form submissions?
faq_plan.a: Have each evaluator score alone first, then put the sheets side by side before the panel meets. A gap of 10 points or more on one criterion is the item worth discussing. With Emergent, the score sheets live in a database you own, next to the proposals they rate.

faq_plan.q: Can an RFP form collect payment before vendors get the documents?
faq_plan.a: Yes, you can build that. Put a payment form in front of the RFP package, and the app releases the documents once the payment goes through. The app connects to Stripe or another payment tool through its API, and each payment lands on the vendor's registration record. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, however many vendors register.

plan.angle: The top 10 is RFP document templates and process guides: agency PDFs (FHWA, USAC, Utah schools, ASU), Indeed, BMC, HubSpot and Investopedia. Every one stops at the document the buyer writes. None shows the form side of an RFP: where vendor proposals arrive, how the question period stays fair, how a department asks procurement to open an RFP, and how evaluators score what came in. This page shows those four moments with real numbers, and answers what a buyer asks while setting one up: what the form should hold, how long to keep it open, what to do with a late proposal.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an RFP Form That Takes Proposals Until the Deadline'; hero 'Build an RFP form that takes technical and price proposals until the deadline and saves each one to a database you own.' covers the whole job (intake, cutoff, storage); how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is RFP templates and process guides; AMBER angle (vendor-response form, not the document) carried throughout, and FAQ 3 'What should an RFP form template include?' answers the template intent with five concrete parts.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'addendum acknowledgment', 'price proposal as its own upload', 'RFP 26-014 closes at 2:00 PM', 'Evaluators score technical approach out of 40'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on actions or events: 'Ask for the technical proposal...', 'RFP 26-014 closes at 2:00 PM on its due date.', 'Three proposals came in for the gate cameras...'.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; one 36-word sentence in FAQ 6 kept as a note.

voice.evidence: Calm, specific operator voice: 'At 2:00 PM the submit button turns off for every vendor.' Regulation wording lifted into FAQ 1 and 5 kept as a note.

truth.evidence: Two FAR statements drop the qualifier their own source carries: FAQ 5 'Federal agencies shall allow at least a 30-day response time ... when the contract is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold' (FAR 5.203(c) excepts commercial products and services); howto_step_6_des 'A federal RFP states the factors used to evaluate proposals and their relative importance' (FAR 15.203(a) applies this to RFPs for competitive acquisitions). Other FAR lines (FAQ 1, 6, 8) are scoped to federal purchasing and match their quotes; private buyers are told they set their own rule. Table cells match rules/competitors/form.json; 34+26+27=87 agrees in copy and image.

distinct.evidence: Own stories (Winslade USD, Bexley Parks question period, Cordova request intake, Ferrand scoring); no sibling primary in a heading; sponsorship form is linked in an answer, not targeted.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, PAA gate 10 pass 0 reject, verbatim Q1 ok, hub link in item 2, links to sponsorship-form, booking-form, payment-form; no brand or format in any question; no legal-advice question.

findings.quote: For a large federal contract, at least 30 days. Federal agencies shall allow at least a 30-day response time for receipt of bids or proposals when the contract is expected to exceed the simplified acquisition threshold.
findings.issue: FAR 5.203(c) opens 'Except for the acquisition of commercial products or commercial services'; the quoted span in domain_sources was cut just after that exception, and the page states the 30-day minimum as applying to every federal contract above the threshold. The spec's own claim line records the exception; the copy drops it, so the source does not say what the page says.
findings.fix: Restore the exception in both sentences, e.g. 'For a federal contract above the simplified acquisition threshold, at least 30 days, unless the purchase is commercial products or services. FAR 5.203 sets that minimum from the day the solicitation is issued.' Keep the private-purchase sentence as is. Extend the domain_sources quote to include the 'Except for...' clause.

findings.quote: A federal RFP states the factors used to evaluate proposals and their relative importance, and vendors write their proposals to those factors.
findings.issue: FAR 15.203(a) requires this of 'RFPs for competitive acquisitions', and the spec's own claim line says 'for a competitive acquisition'; the copy generalises it to every federal RFP (sole-source RFPs are not covered).
findings.fix: Write 'A competitive federal RFP states the factors used to evaluate proposals and their relative importance...' (or 'In a competitive federal acquisition, the RFP states...'). Check the step stays within 35-50 words.
